stem.en: Kabir asks why the bacterium "does not just always make a little cutter, to be safe". What does the sim's coin counter say?

text.en: Making an unneeded enzyme costs coins and beads every hour, and a bacterium that saves them divides faster than one that does not. A cell that spends on nothing loses the race to one that spends on what is there.

feedback.en: Ready costs. In a bath with no lactose, the always-on cell spends coins on nothing and grows slower.

text.en: It cannot make a little; it is on or off.

feedback.en: The repressor lets go in proportion to lactose, so the gene runs at a level between off and full. The point is that zero lactose gives nearly zero.
The cutter without its substrate does nothing. The cost is the waste, not poison.

explanation.en: Every protein costs coins to make. A switch that makes it only when it can earn its keep is a cheaper cell, and cheaper cells win.
